Surfaces

The containers content sits on. What separates one from another is its FILL, not an outline or a shadow: a card is a block of color a step away from the page, and three cards in a row read as three cards because of the gaps between three blocks of color.

Cards

One subject per card. A card is made of optional slots — media, header, body, actions — used in whatever combination the content needs.

M2

Filled

The default card

Its own fill is the whole mechanism — no shadow, no border, in any state. A resting card that casts a shadow is the clearest tell of a different design language.
O

Outlined

Retired — now an alias

It used to give up its fill for a hairline, to bound a block without reading as a surface of its own. That distinction does not exist in a language where being bounded is being a surface, and a grid of hairline cards inside a kit where nothing else has an edge reads as a second kit rather than as a quieter card. So this is the base card now. The class stays so markup keeps working.
F

Flat

One step up

A rung further up the ladder, where a card is nested inside another card and the parent has already spent the surface fill.

Expansion panels

Built on details and summary, so expanding works with no script at all and the content is still findable by the browser's own search.

What is in this kit?
Every element a page is likely to need: buttons, fields, selection controls, navigation, surfaces, feedback, data display, media and long-form content.
Can I use it without a build step?
Yes. There are three files — one page, one stylesheet, one script — and no dependencies beyond two webfonts.
How do I change the design language?
Replace design_language.css. As long as the replacement defines the same token names and the same class contract, the markup on every page keeps working.

Dividers

A hairline is the lightest way to group. Reach for whitespace first and a divider only when the grouping is genuinely ambiguous.

Sheets

A surface that slides in from an edge. The bottom sheet is the touch-friendly alternative to a menu; the side sheet holds filters and detail panes.

Plain surfaces

When none of the named components fit, .surface plus a rung of the fill ladder is the raw material everything else is built from. The elevation classes still exist, but they are for things that genuinely float.
